modelResponse.episodeSummary: 64F with sudden onset atrial flutter and hypotension, likely secondary to flecainide-induced conduction abnormality.
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Wide bizarre QRS not conforming to typical RBBB or LBBB pattern; 1:1 AV conduction; flutter waves faintly visible
preEventNote: QRS wider than baseline (baseline QRS 88 ms per prior ECG)
modelResponse.mechanism: Flecainide, a Class IC antiarrhythmic, can cause significant widening of the QRS complex and facilitate 1:1 AV conduction in atrial flutter, leading to rapid ventricular response and hemodynamic compromise.
contributingFactors: Flecainide started 2 weeks ago without AV nodal blocker co-prescribed
Blood pressure: 88/54 mmHg (MAP 65 mmHg) - borderline hypotensive

rejectedAlternatives.why: Rhythm is regular and shows flutter waves distorting ST segments; QRS morphology is more consistent with atrial flutter with 1:1 conduction.
Presence of flutter waves and specific history of flecainide initiation makes atrial flutter more likely.

recommendedActions: Immediate 12-lead ECG and continuous cardiac monitoring
Assess for signs of shock or pulmonary edema
Administer intravenous fluids to support blood pressure (BP 88/54)
Consult Cardiology for management of flecainide-induced arrhythmia
Consider rapid cardioversion if hemodynamically unstable
uncertainty: QRS duration is 'N/A' due to being obscured by wide QRS, making precise measurement difficult
Troponin T 0.02 ng/mL is 'mild HIGH (demand)', but lacks specific diagnostic weight in this acute setting
